content: This resulted in a final analytic sample of 136,652 women. Interventions Information on parity and breastfeeding characteristics was collected at baseline in the Women’s Health Initiative using self-administered questionnaires. Data included the number of pregnancies, number of term pregnancies, age at first term pregnancy, whether the participant breastfed a child for at least one month, the number of children breastfed, age at first and last breastfeeding, and total months of breastfeeding. Outcomes The primary outcome was the incidence of diabetes during follow-up, determined through self-reported new diagnoses of diabetes treated with insulin or oral hypoglycemic medications. Lupton 2013 This cross-sectional study used data from women participating in the 45 and Up Study in Australia. Participants were randomly selected from the Australian Medicare Database and completed a baseline questionnaire. Inclusion criteria included women aged 45 years or older who had given birth after the age of 18 and before 45, with no history of hysterectomy or bilateral oophorectomy. Breastfeeding duration was calculated by dividing the total breastfeeding duration by the number of children breastfed. Maguire 2013 This cross-sectional study involved healthy urban children aged 1 to 6 years attending routine primary healthcare in Toronto, Canada, between December 2008 and June 2011. Participants were recruited from seven pediatric and family medicine practices. Inclusion criteria included healthy children attending routine care, while exclusion criteria included chronic health conditions (except asthma) or evidence of inflammation (CRP >10 mg/L). Interventions Data were collected prospectively using standardized parent-completed surveys. Breastfeeding duration was categorized as 0 months for those who never breastfed, and for those currently breastfeeding, the duration was equal to the child’s current age. Outcomes Iron deficiency was defined as serum ferritin levels below 14 mcg/L. Martin 2002 The Carnegie survey, conducted between 1937 and 1939 in Britain, was a cross-sectional study of diet, social circumstances, and health. Data on childhood anthropometry and infant feeding methods were recorded for 2,995 subjects from 1,072 families. Interventions Mothers provided information on infant feeding methods and breastfeeding duration, categorized into time intervals (e.g., two weeks to less than two months, more than two to less than six months, etc.). Outcomes Mean differences in z-scores for height, trunk length, and leg length were analyzed. Michels 1996 This prospective cohort study followed 89,887 women from the Nurses’ Health Study cohort between 1986 and 1992. Exclusion criteria included women who died before 1986, reported any cancer (except non-melanoma skin cancer) between 1978 and 1986, were nulliparous in 1984, or had unknown parity or breastfeeding history. Interventions Cumulative breastfeeding duration was categorized into groups (e.g., never, less than one month, up to 48 months). Miyake 2007 The Ryukyus Child Health Study analyzed data from 24,077 schoolchildren aged 6 to 15 years in Okinawa, Japan, between September 2004 and January 2005. Health data were collected via questionnaires completed by parents or students. Outcomes The prevalence of allergic disorders, including wheezing, atopic eczema, and rhinoconjunctivitis, was assessed based on specific symptoms reported in the past 12 months. Muniz 2015 This prospective cohort study included all live births from 1982 and 1993 in Pelotas, Brazil. Participants from the 1982 birth cohort and a subsample of the 1993 cohort with complete breastfeeding data were analyzed. Interventions Breastfeeding information was collected prospectively during the first four years of life through home interviews with mothers. Mwakayoka 2017 This cross-sectional study in Mbeya City, Tanzania, used quota sampling based on rural-urban strata and age distribution of children aged 2 to 4 years. Mothers and children were interviewed about demographic characteristics, breastfeeding, and weaning practices. Interventions Breastfeeding duration was recorded and categorized into one year, more than one year up to two years, and more than two years. N’gandu 1990 This cross-sectional study surveyed randomly selected households in an urban township in Lusaka, Zambia. Mothers or close relatives provided information on breastfeeding duration, defined as the age at which breastfeeding completely stopped. Nam 2019 This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) from 2010 to 2013. Data from 9,960 parous women were analyzed after excluding individuals with missing data, nulliparous women, and those diagnosed with diabetes before their first delivery. Interventions Breastfeeding history and total breastfeeding duration were assessed, with participants categorized into groups based on total and average breastfeeding duration. Nambiar 2013 This cross-sectional study used data from the Healthy Kids Queensland Physical Activity and Nutrition Survey (2006). Parents provided information on early feeding behaviors and anthropometry. Nandi 2017 This cohort study used data from the Andhra Pradesh Children and Parents Study (APCAPS) and the India Human Development Surveys (IHDS). Breastfeeding duration was categorized into groups based on months of breastfeeding. Nord-Trøndelag Health Study (HUNT) This population-based health survey in Norway included adults over 19 years of age. Exclusion criteria included non-response to questionnaires, current pregnancy, age over 85 years, and self-reported pre-existing conditions such as diabetes or cardiovascular disease. Interventions Lifetime lactation duration was calculated and categorized into five levels (e.g., none, 1–6 months, etc.). Neutzling 2009 This prospective cohort study followed participants from the 1993 Pelotas Birth Cohort in Brazil. Breastfeeding duration and the introduction of solid or semi-solid foods were assessed. Nguyen 2019 The 45 and Up Study in New South Wales, Australia, included women aged 45 years or older. Exclusion criteria included nulliparity and recent cardiovascular disease diagnoses. Interventions Breastfeeding duration was categorized into groups (e.g., never, less than six months, etc.). Nirunsittirat 2016 This cohort study followed 860 children from the Prospective Cohort Study of Thai Children (PCTC) in Thailand. Breastfeeding practices were categorized into exclusive, full, and any breastfeeding, with duration categorized into four groups (<6 months, 6–11 months, etc.). Novaes 2012 This cross-sectional study in Brazil included children aged 6 to 10 years. Mothers provided information on family characteristics, pregnancy conditions, and breastfeeding duration. Nseroko 2018 This cross-sectional study used data from the 2010 Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey. Breastfeeding practices were assessed based on WHO indicators, including early initiation, exclusive breastfeeding under six months, and continued breastfeeding at one year. Nunes 2012 This retrospective cohort study in Brazil analyzed preschool children from low-income populations. Breastfeeding duration and early childhood caries (ECC) were assessed.
